items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Bob was in the booth and his engineer, a guy named Eddie Bracken, I’ll never forget him

ctx.x: But when you got to the point where you had a reputation and you were doing solo recordings, I’m wondering how much thought did you give to fitting into what niche? Was it going to be jazz-rock, was it — or maybe this didn’t even occur to you. Maybe you were just composing music and looking for tunes that you liked?

Pretty much the latter. I was in New York, I can’t remember why, but I got to see Bob Thiele in his office at Impulse Records at the time, and it was time to do another, a second album. And he said, “Tom what do you want to do?” And I said, “I want to do a jazz album with my quartet” which at the time was Mike Lang on piano, Chuck Domanico on bass and John Guerin on drums. And so he said, “Cool.” So back in Los Angeles I walked into United Recording Studio. Bob was in the booth and his engineer, a guy named Eddie…
